About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Electronics and Mechatronics
Years 12–13 of the New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Electronics and Mechatronics Years 12–13
is still in development. Once that is completed, Electronics and Mechatronics Years
12–13 is proposed to be made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum
Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Electronics and Mechatronics Years 12–13 will be required to start using it
in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13 from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.




Electronics and Mechatronics | Years 12–13 | October 2026                               Page 2

Purpose statement
                                                                        Tukuna a whakaaro auaha kia rere kia                 Through creativity and innovation, we
                                                                        whakaumutia ai te ao.                                intervene to transform the world.




  In Electronics and Mechatronics, students are taught about processes such as                Electronics and Mechatronics leads to pathways in engineering, communication
  circuit design, managing signals and power, using both analogue and digital                 systems, robotics, electronics, industrial and product design, trades, or applied
  methods. They are also taught about mechatronic processes such as sensing,                  technologies.
  actuation, and system integration, and how these approaches enable the creation
  of intelligent engineering systems and apply systems thinking to contexts such as
  robotics, automation, smart devices, and sustainable technologies in
  New Zealand and globally.

Through the study of Year 12–13 Electronics and Mechatronics students are taught to
apply engineering principles to investigate problems and opportunities, and to design,
test, and refine integrated systems. They learn to use iterative processes to analyse
system behaviour, evaluate performance, and develop innovative solutions that
respond effectively to stakeholder needs.

Electronics and Mechatronics provides students with the knowledge and practices to
reason how technological systems operate within social, cultural, and environmental
contexts. Students learn to make informed engineering decisions by considering
system constraints, trade-offs, and evidence gathered through modelling, testing, and
evaluation.

As students progress through Years 12–13 Electronics and Mechatronics, they further
develop their understanding of failure and malfunction as valuable sources of
information that support ongoing improvement and system optimisation. They develop
the ability to use feedback from sensor data, algorithmic or AI-enabled systems,
testing, and users to refine designs, while engaging in design processes that ensure
solutions are shaped by the needs, experiences, and perspectives of those who will
use or be affected by them.

 Disciplinary writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within Electronics and Mechatronics.

 In Electronics and Mechatronics, writing is an analytical and reflective practice that enables students to develop and refine ideas while communicating informed understandings of solutions.
